text:
On process, Utah is as good as anyone right now. The Mammoth have taken 58% of the expected goals at five on five, create 3.58 expected goals per 60 minutes and allow 2.79. They won the chance battle in four of their last five. They are 2-2-1 in that stretch anyway, outscored 19-15, and the reason has a name. Karel Vejmelka is at .826 over his last five starts, 8.3 goals worse than expected, and 1-4-0. Thursday in Montreal, Logan Cooley scored three and Utah still lost 5-4 in overtime after leading by two.

Cooley is the bright side: 15 points in his last ten, earned by chances, not bounces. Clayton Keller has seven assists in a four-game point streak and has taken Kailer Yamamoto's spot beside Hayton and Lee. Vincent Trocheck is one assist from 400. With John Marino out, Andrew Peeke has jumped to 20:09 a night and Mikhail Sergachev to 25:40, which is a lot of hockey.

Ottawa comes home after five straight on the road, closing it with a 2-1 win in Buffalo that ended the Sabres' three-game streak. The Senators are thin: William Eklund is out until January, and Ridly Greig, Andre Burakovsky and Warren Foegele are also missing. Tim Stützle has moved beside Dylan Cozens and Zetterlund, and Shane Pinto plays his 300th NHL game. Samuel Ersson (.880, -0.9 this season) has been ordinary, but next to Vejmelka's month he looks steady.

Watch the penalty box. Ottawa takes 4.9 penalties a game, and Utah's power play creates 0.83 expected goals a game against a Senators kill that allows 0.87. Both teams have 21 points. Our numbers lean Utah, 3.22 expected goals to 3.14, with an 86% playoff chance against Ottawa's 67%.
headline: Utah keeps winning the shots and losing the goalie battle

hunch.text: Our numbers trust Utah's process, and so do we, over a season. Over one night, a goalie at .826 across five starts can slump one more time: our hunch is Ottawa wins at home.
